alternatives.name: Proton Mail
alternatives.summary: Privacy-oriented email with encrypted-message features and open-source clients.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Encryption depends on recipient and message path; account, delivery, and some routing metadata still exist. Some features are paid.

alternatives.name: Thunderbird for Android
alternatives.summary: Open-source email client that can connect to mail providers you choose.
alternatives.tradeoffs: A client does not make the mailbox provider private or add end-to-end encryption to ordinary email by itself.

alternatives.name: Proton Drive
alternatives.summary: Encrypted cloud storage with a first-party Android app.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Still depends on a cloud account and provider availability; sharing links and account recovery need careful handling.

alternatives.name: Nextcloud Files
alternatives.summary: Open-source client for a Nextcloud server that you or an organization choose.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Privacy depends on the server operator, server configuration, and transport; a self-hosted server requires maintenance and backups.

alternatives.name: Ente Photos
alternatives.summary: Photo backup built around end-to-end encryption, with mobile and desktop clients.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Cloud backup still relies on an account and available storage; encryption does not remove visible image content or guarantee every metadata field is scrubbed.

alternatives.name: Organic Maps
alternatives.summary: Offline-first maps and navigation with open map data.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Offline maps are not a full replacement for live traffic, business updates, transit coverage, or every location search. Download map regions in advance.

alternatives.name: OsmAnd
alternatives.summary: Offline-capable maps and navigation with downloadable map data and detailed route options.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Some features and map downloads may be limited by the edition; online search and online services have different privacy properties from offline navigation.

alternatives.name: Firefox for Android
alternatives.summary: Open-source browser with tracking protection controls and add-on support.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Browser privacy depends on settings, extensions, sync choices, and websites visited; it is not anonymous by default.

alternatives.name: Brave Browser
alternatives.summary: Browser with built-in tracker and ad blocking controls.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Optional features and sync choices change behavior; built-in blocking is not a guarantee that all tracking or fingerprinting is prevented.

alternatives.name: DuckDuckGo Privacy Browser
alternatives.summary: Mobile browser centered on DuckDuckGo search and privacy protections.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Search results and browser features differ from Google; using a privacy-oriented browser does not make every visited website private.

alternatives.name: NewPipe
alternatives.summary: Open-source video client that can browse supported services without the official YouTube app.
alternatives.tradeoffs: It is not an official YouTube client; service changes can temporarily break it, and account-based features or DRM content may be unavailable.

alternatives.name: LibreTube
alternatives.summary: Open-source alternative client for browsing YouTube content through configurable Piped instances.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Instance availability, latency, and operator trust vary; the instance may see request metadata. It is not an official YouTube client.

alternatives.name: Etar Calendar
alternatives.summary: Open-source calendar app for local calendars and supported Android calendar providers.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Sync depends on the account/provider configured on Android; replacing the UI alone does not stop a Google account from syncing calendar data.

alternatives.name: Proton Calendar
alternatives.summary: Calendar service with a privacy-focused account model and encrypted data handling.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Requires a Proton account; interoperability, shared calendars, invitations, and features can differ from Google Calendar.

alternatives.name: Joplin
alternatives.summary: Open-source notes and to-do app with local storage and optional sync choices.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Sync encryption and privacy depend on configuration and chosen sync target; verify settings before storing sensitive notes.

alternatives.name: AnySoftKeyboard
alternatives.summary: Open-source Android keyboard with configurable layouts and dictionaries.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Any keyboard can see text typed into fields it serves; avoid optional network/dictionary features unless you understand their data flow.

alternatives.name: Aegis Authenticator
alternatives.summary: Open-source authenticator with an encrypted local vault and export/backup options.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Plan and test an encrypted backup before changing phones; losing the vault and recovery material can lock you out of accounts.

alternatives.name: Fossify Contacts
alternatives.summary: Local-first contacts app from the Fossify open-source app suite.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Contacts sync is separate from the local contacts UI; choose a sync provider consciously and export a backup before migrating.

alternatives.name: F-Droid
alternatives.summary: Repository client focused on free and open-source Android apps, with source/build metadata.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Its catalogue is narrower than Google Play; installing APKs from individual websites without the client can reduce update and signature-change warnings.

alternatives.name: Aurora Store
alternatives.summary: Alternative open-source client for accessing Google Play catalogue listings.
alternatives.tradeoffs: It still accesses the Google Play ecosystem and is not an audit of each app. Account mode, network metadata, and distribution source affect the privacy tradeoff.

alternatives.name: Signal
alternatives.summary: Private messaging with end-to-end encryption for Signal conversations by default.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Both parties need Signal for Signal's encrypted messaging; SMS and other communication paths are not magically converted into Signal E2EE.

alternatives.name: SimpleX Chat
alternatives.summary: Messaging app designed to work without requiring a phone number as a user identifier.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Contacts must also use the service; private routing does not make every device, backup, notification, or recipient endpoint risk disappear.

alternatives.name: Jitsi Meet
alternatives.summary: Video meeting client for Jitsi-compatible meeting services, including self-hosted deployments.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Privacy depends on the chosen server, room configuration, and whether end-to-end encryption is supported and enabled for the participants.

alternatives.name: Bitwarden
alternatives.summary: Password manager with audited security documentation and encrypted vault sync.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Account access and recovery are still critical; use a unique master password and retain recovery/export material securely.

alternatives.name: KeePassDX
alternatives.summary: Open-source password manager for locally stored KeePass-compatible vault files.
alternatives.tradeoffs: You must manage secure vault storage, backup, and synchronization; a lost or corrupted vault can be unrecoverable.

alternatives.name: Feeder
alternatives.summary: Open-source RSS reader for following publications directly instead of a personalized news feed.
alternatives.tradeoffs: You choose the feeds and may miss algorithmically recommended stories; feeds can expose request metadata to the publisher or feed host.

alternatives.name: Translate You
alternatives.summary: Open-source translation client that can connect to supported translation services.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Translation text is sent to whichever provider is configured; the client itself does not make third-party translation services private.

alternatives.name: Collabora Office
alternatives.summary: Office document editor based on LibreOffice technology for working with compatible documents on Android.
alternatives.tradeoffs: The editing app does not automatically provide shared real-time collaboration or a private cloud; storage, sharing, and sync choices are separate.

alternatives.name: Firefox with a user-chosen search engine
alternatives.summary: Use Firefox and select a search provider rather than keeping the Google Search app as the primary search surface.
alternatives.tradeoffs: The selected search provider still receives queries; privacy depends on the provider and your account/sign-in settings.
